$comment: GENERATED by scf-core/scripts/build_negative.mjs. The negative fixtures of spec/conformance.md §5.3. Each case: start from an empty conforming database (spec/scf-schema.sql, plus the header stamps and _scf_meta.schema_version of §1.2), apply `statements` in order, then validate. The result must match the case's <name>.expected.json.

cases.name: uuid-missing
cases.about: A row with no uuid. Nothing can track it across a file.
statements: INSERT INTO scene (name, uuid) VALUES ('INT. VOID', NULL)

cases.name: uuid-duplicate
cases.about: Two rows sharing a uuid. Lineage becomes ambiguous.
statements: DROP INDEX IF EXISTS idx_scene_uuid
INSERT INTO scene (name, uuid) VALUES ('A', ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"]
INSERT INTO scene (name, uuid) VALUES ('B', ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"]

cases.name: uuid-malformed
cases.about: A uuid that is not uuid-shaped.
statements: INSERT INTO scene (name, uuid) VALUES ('C', 'not-a-uuid')

cases.name: relationship-endpoint-absent
cases.about: A relationship pointing at a character that is not here.
statements: INSERT INTO character (name, uuid) VALUES ('ELEANOR', ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"]
INSERT INTO character_relationship (character_a_id, character_b_id, directionality, uuid) VALUES (1, 404, 'mutual', ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002"]

cases.name: relationship-contradictory
cases.about: One pair described as both mutual and directed. No tool can pick the winner — the case §6.5's directionality flag exists for.
statements: INSERT INTO character (name, uuid) VALUES ('ELEANOR', ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"]
INSERT INTO character (name, uuid) VALUES ('MARCUS', ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002"]
INSERT INTO character_relationship (character_a_id, character_b_id, directionality, uuid) VALUES (1, 2, 'mutual', ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003"]
INSERT INTO character_relationship (character_a_id, character_b_id, directionality, uuid) VALUES (1, 2, 'a_to_b', ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000004"]

cases.name: relationship-directionality-absent
cases.about: A relationship with no symmetry fact. Readable, but nothing can tell a duplicate from a second direction. Note the explicit NULL: the column defaults to 'mutual', so this state is only reachable by clearing it — which is exactly what an import from a tool that has no such concept would do.
statements: INSERT INTO character (name, uuid) VALUES ('ELEANOR', ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"]
INSERT INTO character (name, uuid) VALUES ('MARCUS', ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002"]
INSERT INTO character_relationship (character_a_id, character_b_id, directionality, uuid) VALUES (1, 2, NULL, ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000003"]

cases.name: span-boundary-dangling
cases.about: An act anchored to a scene that is not present. Structure must still derive (§5.5) and say so.
statements: INSERT INTO scene (name, scene_number, uuid) VALUES ('INT. KITCHEN', '1', ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"]
INSERT INTO act (name, act_number, start_scene_id, uuid) VALUES ('Act I', 1, 999, ?)   -- params: ["00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000002"]

cases.name: asset-escapes-root
cases.about: An identifier containing '..'. It cannot be resolved, and a resolver that followed it would leave the project.
statements: INSERT INTO asset (name, identifier, uuid) VALUES (?, ?, ?)   -- params: ["escape","@project/../../etc/passwd","00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"]

cases.name: asset-absolute
cases.about: An absolute identifier. Representable on purpose (§8.2), non-portable, and a warning rather than an error.
statements: INSERT INTO asset (name, identifier, uuid) VALUES (?, ?, ?)   -- params: ["plate","/Volumes/plates/sh010.exr","00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000001"]

cases.name: unknown-table
cases.about: A table SCF does not define. Preserved and ignored (§10.1) — reported at info, because unknown usually means historical.
statements: CREATE TABLE legacy_pipeline (k TEXT, v TEXT)
INSERT INTO legacy_pipeline (k, v) VALUES ('shotgun_id', 'sg-1')

cases.name: header-unstamped
cases.about: No application id. Every file written before schema 2.10 looks like this, and a reader MUST NOT refuse it (§1.2).
statements: PRAGMA application_id = 0
PRAGMA user_version = 0
